_comment: The guild-name equality contract, as ONE table read by both readers of data/guild-config.json.
bnet.sync.same_guild (the nightly: which guild rosters to fetch and auto-add) and
js/state.js guildNameEquals (the site: which rows the scope admits, and which chip they land on)
must answer identically for every pair, because a scope the two readers disagree about is silent:
the nightly appends members the site then never lists, and a chip can strand rows it owns.
test_sidecar_phase_c.py asserts same_guild() against this table; verify_search_detail.mjs asserts
guildNameEquals() against the same file; verify_sync_artifacts.py gates the file's existence, shape
and consumption by both. Add the pair here when a rule changes — never by editing one side.
Rule, in words: trim, case-fold, drop every character outside letters/digits, and compare that — one
comparison, not exact-then-forgiving. A name that squashes away to nothing ("---") is not a name and
matches nothing, not even itself. A Blizzard guild slug is its display name with the punctuation
flattened, which is why 'twelve-guards' IS 'Twelve Guards'.
Neither reader folds composed and decomposed accents, so the NFC/NFD pair below is FALSE on
purpose: it is a known limit written down, not an oversight.
One limit neither reader can share, so it is written here rather than tested: Python casefold()
folds 'ss' from 'sz' and from the sharp s, while JS toLowerCase() leaves 'ss' alone. A pair like
('Straße','Strasse') is therefore equal to the nightly and unequal to the site. No guild name in
this roster (or in Blizzard's forever-us index today) contains one, so the pair is out of the
table on purpose: a table entry Python passes and JS fails would be a lie about one of them.

cases.why: case is not part of a guild's identity
the config value and a typed name are both trimmed
the slug form of a display name (the reason the squash exists)
spaces are punctuation too — the deliberate cost of accepting slugs
a different guild, not a prefix match
an empty name never scopes to a real guild
not even empty matches empty: a blank scope means unscoped
punctuation alone squashes to empty, which matches nothing
two empty squashes are still no name
NFC vs NFD: documented non-goal, both readers leave it distinct
the rule is about names, not about this file
punctuation alone is not a name, so it matches nothing — including itself; an exact-match shortcut would say True here and js/state.js would say False
